# TASK 1
## Rationale
A few of the prices were a very expensive items therefore I use the log scale for the histogram along with the line of the mean and the median to understand the graph better. I also join the orderItems to products and remove the NA items so that the plot could be drawn without a problem. 

### Question 1
* Visualize the distribution of item prices in order_items.csv with a histogram, and report the mean and median price.

```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

orderItems = read.csv("order_items.csv")
products = read.csv("products.csv")
orders = read.csv("orders.csv")
customers = read.csv("customers.csv")
payments = read.csv("payments.csv")

```

```{r}
meanPrice = mean(orderItems$price)
medianPrice = median(orderItems$price)
cat("Mean:", round(meanPrice, 2), " Median:", round(medianPrice, 2))
```
```{r}
priceHist = ggplot(data = orderItems) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = price), bins = 50) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = meanPrice, colour = "pink") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = medianPrice, colour = "purple") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of item prices",
       x = "Price", y = "Number of items")
print(priceHist)
```

### Question 2
* Join order_items.csv and products.csv, and draw a scatter plot of freight value against product weight (product_weight_g). Describe the relationship.

```{r}
itemsProducts = orderItems %>% inner_join(products, by = "product_id")
cat("NA datas:", sum(is.na(itemsProducts$product_weight_g)))
```
```{r, message = FALSE}
plotData = itemsProducts %>% filter(!is.na(product_weight_g))

freightPoint = ggplot(data = plotData,
  mapping = aes(x = product_weight_g, y = freight_value)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Freight value against product weight",
       x = "Product weight", y = "Freight value")
print(freightPoint)
```

### Findings.
The mean price is higher than the median and this is because some of the expensive items pulled it up. The freight goes up as the weight also goes up, but as we can see the points are mostly spread out, therefore weight is not the only variable that matters.
